name: Windows-MCP
description: MCP Server that enables Claude to interact with Windows OS
long_description:
Windows-MCP is an open-source project that enables seamless integration between AI agents and the Windows operating system. Acting as an MCP server, it bridges the gap between large language models (LLMs) and the Windows OS, allowing agents to perform tasks such as **file navigation, application control, UI interaction, QA testing, and more**.

**KEY FEATURES**
- **Seamless Windows Integration**: Interacts natively with Windows UI elements, opens applications, controls windows, simulates user input, and more.
- **Use Any LLM (Vision Optional)**: Does not rely on traditional computer vision techniques or fine-tuned models. Works with any LLM, reducing complexity and setup time.
- **Rich Toolset for UI Automation**: Includes tools for keyboard and mouse control, window management, and capturing window or UI state.
- **Lightweight & Open-Source**: Minimal dependencies with full source code available under the MIT license.
- **Customizable & Extendable**: Easily adapt or extend tools to suit custom automation workflows or AI integrations.
- **Real-Time Interaction**: Typical latency between actions ranges from `0.2` to `0.9` seconds, depending on system load, active applications, and LLM inference speed.

**MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS**
- **Python 3.14+**

anonymized_telemetry.title: Anonymized Telemetry
anonymized_telemetry.description: Windows-MCP collects basic usage data to help improve the MCP server. No personal information, tool arguments, or tool outputs are tracked.

profile_snapshot.title: Profile Snapshot Performance
profile_snapshot.description: Enable detailed performance logging for desktop snapshots and screenshots in the server console/logs. Useful for troubleshooting latency.

screenshot_backend.title: Screenshot Backend
screenshot_backend.description: The engine used to capture screenshots. 'auto' automatically selects the fastest available backend (DXGI -> MSS -> Pillow). Use 'pillow' if you encounter capture issues.

debug.title: Debug Mode
debug.description: Enable debug mode to provide verbose logging for troubleshooting.

watchdog.title: UIA Focus WatchDog
watchdog.description: Run the UIAutomation focus watchdog. Off by default: it currently only emits debug logging, while costing a background thread and a UIA event subscription that can crash the server on unstable UIA environments. Tool behaviour is unaffected either way.

tools.name: ControlStatus
tools.description: Reports whether AI or the user currently controls the desktop and the remaining user-idle wait before AI control can resume. This read-only status remains available during user takeover. Also reports server elevation (is_admin/integrity/UAC) and the elevated worker state.

tools.name: App
tools.description: Manages Windows applications with three modes: 'launch' (opens the prescibed application), 'resize' (adjusts the size/position of a named window or the active window if name is omitted), 'switch' (brings specific window into focus).

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description: A comprehensive system tool for executing any PowerShell commands. Use it to navigate the file system, manage files and processes, and execute system-level operations. Capable of accessing web content, interacting with network resources, and performing complex administrative tasks. Set elevated=true to run with administrator rights (install software, services, HKLM, firewall, scheduled tasks, Program Files) via a persistent elevated worker.

tools.name: FileSystem
tools.description: Manages file system operations with eight modes: 'read' (read text file contents), 'write' (create/overwrite/append to files), 'copy' (copy files or directories), 'move' (move or rename), 'delete' (delete files or directories), 'list' (list directory contents), 'search' (find files by glob pattern), 'info' (get metadata like size, dates, type). Relative paths are resolved from the user's Desktop folder. Use absolute paths to access other locations. Set elevated=true to read/write in admin-only locations like Program Files.

tools.name: Screenshot
tools.description: Captures a fast screenshot-first desktop snapshot with cursor position, active/open windows, and an image. Skips UI tree extraction for speed and should be the default first call when you mainly need visual context. Supports display=[0] or display=[0,1] using zero-based active Windows display indices. Set save_path to an absolute file or directory path to also write the image to disk; the saved path is reported in the result. Note: the returned image may be downscaled for efficiency; when it is, multiply image coordinates by the ratio of original size to displayed size to get the actual screen coordinates for mouse actions (Click, Move, etc.).

tools.name: Snapshot
tools.description: Captures complete desktop state including: system language, focused/opened windows, interactive elements (buttons, text fields, links, menus with coordinates), and scrollable areas. Use this when you need interactive element ids, scrollable regions, or browser DOM extraction with use_dom=True. Set use_vision=True to include screenshot. Set display=[0] or display=[0,1] using zero-based active Windows display indices; omit it to keep the default full-desktop behavior. Set save_path (with use_vision=True) to an absolute file or directory path to also write the screenshot to disk.

tools.name: DisplayInventory
tools.description: Reads the active display layout and DPI metadata. Reports each display's index, device name, monitor and work-area bounds, resolution, orientation, primary flag, effective DPI, and scale.

tools.name: Click
tools.description: Performs mouse clicks at coordinates [x, y], on a UI element's label/id, or on a target described in words (e.g. 'Save button', 'File > Save As'), resolved in-process from the accessibility tree. On a weak match nothing is clicked and the top candidates are returned.

tools.name: Locate
tools.description: Read-only: finds the UI element a target described in words refers to in the foreground (or named) window and returns the best match with confidence plus the top candidates (name, type, loc, score), without clicking.

tools.name: Type
tools.description: Types text at specified coordinates [x, y] or passing a UI element's label/id. Set clear=True to clear existing text first, False to append. Set press_enter=True to submit after typing. Set caret_position to 'start' (beginning), 'end' (end), or 'idle' (default). Provide either loc or label. clear and press_enter accept only true or false. An empty text types nothing, so combine it with clear=True to just empty a field. Accepts target to name the field in words instead of loc/label.

tools.name: Scroll
tools.description: Scrolls at coordinates [x, y], a UI element's label/id, or current mouse position if loc=None. Type: vertical (default) or horizontal. Direction: up/down for vertical, left/right for horizontal. wheel_times controls amount (1 wheel ≈ 3-5 lines). Use for navigating long content, lists, and web pages.

tools.name: Move
tools.description: Moves mouse cursor to coordinates [x, y] or passing a UI element's label/id. Set drag=True to perform a drag-and-drop operation from the current mouse position to the target coordinates. Default (drag=False) is a simple cursor move (hover). Provide either loc or label.

tools.name: Shortcut
tools.description: Executes keyboard shortcuts using key combinations separated by +. Examples: "ctrl+c" (copy), "ctrl+v" (paste), "alt+tab" (switch apps), "win+r" (Run dialog), "win" (Start menu), "ctrl+shift+esc" (Task Manager). Use for quick actions and system commands.

tools.name: Wait
tools.description: Pauses execution for specified duration in seconds. Use when waiting for: applications to launch/load, UI animations to complete, page content to render, dialogs to appear, or between rapid actions. Helps ensure UI is ready before next interaction.

tools.name: WaitFor
tools.description: Waits until a UI condition is met by polling the accessibility tree inside a single call, avoiding repeated Snapshot calls. Conditions: text_exists, active_window, element_exists, element_enabled, focused_element. Provide text and/or window_name depending on the condition. Set use_dom=True to match browser DOM text.

tools.name: Scrape
tools.description: Fetch content from a URL or the active browser tab. By default, performs a lightweight HTTP request to the URL. If you need to extract text from the active tab's DOM within the viewport, ensure the page is open in a browser and use Snapshot with use_dom=True first, then the agent will handle extraction. Use Screenshot for the default fast visual inspection path.

tools.name: MultiSelect
tools.description: Selects multiple items such as files, folders, or checkboxes if press_ctrl=True, or performs multiple clicks if False. Pass locs (list of coordinates) or labels (list of UI element labels/ids).

tools.name: MultiEdit
tools.description: Enters text into multiple input fields at specified coordinates locs=[[x,y,text], ...] or using labels=[[label,text], ...]. Provide either locs or labels.

tools.name: Clipboard
tools.description: Manages Windows clipboard operations. Use mode="get" to read current clipboard content, mode="set" to set clipboard text.

tools.name: Process
tools.description: Manages system processes. Use mode="list" to list running processes with filtering and sorting options. Use mode="kill" to terminate processes by PID or name. Set elevated=true to kill elevated or other-user processes.

tools.name: Notification
tools.description: Sends a Windows toast notification with a title and message. Optional app_id selects the registered AppUserModelID it appears under (defaults to Windows PowerShell).

tools.name: Registry
tools.description: Accesses the Windows Registry. Use mode="get" to read a value, mode="set" to create/update a value, mode="delete" to remove a value or key, mode="list" to list values and sub-keys under a path. Set elevated=true for HKLM/admin-only writes and deletes.

tools.name: Apps
tools.description: Installed-app inventory merged from the Start menu, AppX packages, uninstall registry keys and URL protocol handlers. mode='list' prints one compact line per app with its skill (if any), URI schemes and process; supports a fuzzy query and limit. mode='info' returns the full record (aliases, AUMID, exe, process names, publisher, version, URI schemes) plus a skill summary. mode='refresh' rebuilds the cached inventory and reloads skills.

tools.name: AppSkill
tools.description: Returns the markdown skill for an app: launch commands and URI deep links, keyboard shortcuts, recipes using these tools, and UI quirks. Resolves by skill name, app name, alias or process name with precedence builtin > user > generated. generate=true builds a skill from the app's menus and accessibility tree when none exists; regenerate=true rebuilds a generated one. Never overwrites builtin or user skills.

tools.name: Context
tools.description: Read-only, fast: the foreground window (title, process, app kind), browser URL and registrable domain, focused field (name, type, is_password), Outlook/webmail To/Cc recipients, and the scam-guard verdict (safe|suspicious|dangerous|unknown, score, brand, reasons) for that site or recipient.

tools.name: CheckLink
tools.description: Read-only, sub-millisecond local phishing/lookalike check of a URL, domain or email address (or a list) before opening a link or sending mail: confusable characters (rnicorsoft.com, paypa1.com), brand in a subdomain (microsoft.com.verify-login.xyz), user@host tricks, risky TLDs. Optional Microsoft-Decision-1 second opinion with OPENROUTER_API_KEY.

tools.name: Browser
tools.description: Fast web automation in Edge/Chrome over the Chrome DevTools Protocol, without screenshots or the OS mouse/keyboard (background-safe, runs alongside screen tools). Attaches to the browser on the debugging port or launches Edge with a persistent profile. Modes: open, search (top results), read (page text + numbered interactive elements), click, fill (one value or a list, optional submit), type, press, eval, wait (returns as soon as text/selector/url holds), screenshot (page JPEG), tabs (list/switch/new/close), back, forward, reload. Every action returns the new url/title and loaded state. Input into a page the scam guard flags needs confirmed=true.

tools.name: Tasks
tools.description: Tracks a multi-step request as a plan of dependent tasks (plan, add, update, next, list, get, cancel, clear, events). 'next' splits ready tasks into a sequential screen lane and a parallel background lane; every change is pushed live as a task_event (MCP log notification, optional JSON-lines file and webhook).

tools.name: RunParallel
tools.description: Runs several tool calls in one turn: background calls (FileSystem, PowerShell, Registry, Process list, App launch, Locate, ...) run concurrently with bounded concurrency and a per-call timeout, while screen calls (Click, Type, Scroll, Move, Shortcut, MultiSelect, MultiEdit, App switch/resize) run one at a time in order through the screen lock. Each inner call passes the same control gate and policy as a direct call; results return in input order with latency and error, and linked tasks update automatically.

tools.name: Do
tools.description: Hands a small concrete desktop goal to a fast model running inside the server (default Claude Haiku 5.5; WINDOWS_MCP_DO_MODEL), which drives a compact subset of the server's own tools (Snapshot, Click/Type by target name, Shortcut, App, Scroll, Wait/WaitFor, PowerShell, AppSkill/Apps, Locate) in-process, so one call does many steps. Every inner call passes the control gate, policy and screen lock; Do holds the screen for its run. Optional decision-model verification of the final screen. Returns a transcript with per-step latency and model/tool/overhead timing; streams do_event progress.

tools.name: Route
tools.description: Scores text against a fixed set of options with a fast decision model (default Microsoft-Decision-1 via OpenRouter's Decisions API; WINDOWS_MCP_ROUTER_MODEL) and returns the choice with calibrated per-option probabilities. Default options for a user utterance: direct_action, needs_plan, answer_only, clarify. mode='verify' checks a step from before/after screen text: succeeded, failed or still_loading.
